description: //patch-automerge is deliberately not extended here, because for this dependency it could never fire. Typesense numbers its stable releases with two components - 26.0, 27.0, 27.1, 28.0, 29.0, 29.1, 30.0, 30.1, 30.2 is the whole stable stream since the 0.25.x era - and Renovate classifies an update by comparing the parsed sections in order (lib/workers/repository/process/lookup/update-type.ts): a differing major is `major`, a differing minor is `minor`, and only what is left over is `patch`. With two components the minor always differs on a real bump, so 30.1 -> 30.2 is a `minor` update and 30.2 -> 31.0 a `major` one, `patch` is unreachable, and `matchUpdateTypes: ["patch"]` matches nothing. Nor is a third component going to appear: Typesense uses that slot for release candidates (`30.2.rc12`), which Renovate's `docker` versioning does not accept as a version at all - and even a hypothetical `30.2.1` would be skipped, because that versioning only considers a candidate compatible when it has the same number of components as the pinned value.

Typesense's own numbering does not agree with that classification - v30.2 'fixes some important bugs identified in v30.1', and v29.1 and v27.1 have the same shape, so the second component really is Typesense's bug-fix level. Making automerge live here would mean saying so explicitly, either with `versioning=regex:^(?<major>\d+)[.](?<patch>\d+)$` on the annotation in defaults/main.yml or with a local packageRule automerging `minor` for this dependency alone. That is a judgement call about what may land unattended on someone's search index, and it has deliberately not been made here rather than made by accident.

What was measured, in case it is made later: Typesense's on-disk format is version-tolerant in both directions, unlike its cousin Meilisearch, which refuses a database written by any other version at all. A collection and a document written by the 29.1 image were read and searched by the 30.2 image over the same data directory - no migration step, no refusal - and the 29.1 image then started again over the directory 30.2 had been using and still found the document. 30.1 -> 30.2 behaves the same. Restarting is otherwise uneventful; /health does answer 503 with `{"ok": false}` for about ten seconds while the single-node Raft group re-elects, and recovers on its own.

The Molecule scenario is what any future automerge would rest on, and it does more than watch the unit turn active (`Restart=always` makes even a crash-looping container report that). It asserts that the version reported by /debug equals the leaf variable Renovate edits, that an unauthenticated and a wrong-key request are both refused, that the API key and the non-default API port the role rendered into `env` are the ones the process is holding, that a document indexed through the API is found by a search that should match and not by one that should not, and that it is all still there after the service is restarted and the container re-created.
